name: makersuite-inline-image
purpose: MAKERSUITE inline image media, the branch that had no fixture at all. Pinned: convertGooglePrompt (src/prompt-converters.js:432) converts a user turn whose content is an ARRAY of parts; `part.type === 'image_url'` takes part.image_url.url and part.image_url.detail and calls addDataUrlPart(url, 'image/png', detail) (:561-564). addDataUrlPart (:515-537) splits the URL on its first comma, takes the mime from `header.match(/data:([^;]+)/)` falling back to the passed default (:518), and pushes `{ inlineData: { mimeType, data } }` with that member order (:521-526). The model is gemini-2.5-pro, which does NOT match /gemini-3/ (:529), so no mediaResolution is attached even though this branch passes detail through -- that is the image sibling of makersuite-inline-video-resolution.json, whose only other difference is the model and the detail level.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider/main.go: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port

tier2.rule: the recorder origin is replaced with <mock>
tier2.reason: API_MAKERSUITE is a pinned literal, so the GoTavern leg reaches the recorder through its seam and the pinned leg through this transport redirect. The PATH and the ?key= parameter are untouched and ARE compared.

tier2.rule: recorded verbatim; the payload is a data: URL, so no authority is substituted and no fetch is involved
tier2.reason: The media reaches the provider INLINE. It is a data: URL on purpose: addDataUrlPart only accepts a url that startsWith('data:') (src/prompt-converters.js:516) and the handler fetches nothing for this source, so the peer receives the exact bytes the pinned converter embedded and the probe cannot reach the network (doctrine 6). A remote http(s) URL here would be silently DROPPED by the same guard rather than fetched, which would make the scenario pass while proving nothing about transport.

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
